questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=4t^2\), find \(v_x\) at \(t=3\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(x(t)=5t-2\), find the instantaneous velocity.
For \(x(t)=2/t\), find \(v_x\) at \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(x(t)=t^3-6t\), find \(v_x\) at \(t=2\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(x(t)=t^2-8t\), when is the particle momentarily at rest?
For \(x(t)=t^3-3t^2\), find the times when the particle is momentarily at rest.
If \(v_x=-7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), what is the speed?
For \(x(t)=-2t^2+12t\), find \(v_x\) at \(t=4\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(x(t)=t^3\), find \(v_x\) at \(t=0\).
If \(v_x>0\), what is happening to \(x(t)\)?
questions.answer: The position is increasing at that instant. The particle is moving in the positive axis direction.

questions.prompt: What does instantaneous velocity represent on a position-time graph?
questions.answer:
It is the slope of the tangent line at one instant:
\[
v_x=\frac{dx}{dt}
\]

questions.prompt: Why are the units of \(dx/dt\) metres per second?
questions.answer:
The numerator has units of metres and the denominator has units of seconds:
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}\rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: What is the difference between instantaneous velocity and speed?
questions.answer:
Instantaneous velocity keeps direction and sign. Speed is its magnitude:
\[
v=|v_x|
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=t^2-4t\), during what time interval is the particle moving in the negative direction?
questions.answer:
\[
v_x=2t-4
\]
Negative motion occurs when
\[
2t-4<0
\]
\[
t<2\,\mathrm{s}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=A\cos(\omega t)\), find \(v_x(t)\).
For \(x(t)=10-3t\), find the velocity and state the direction of motion.
questions.answer:
\[
v_x=-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The particle moves in the negative axis direction.

questions.prompt: How is instantaneous velocity related to average velocity over smaller and smaller intervals?
questions.answer:
It is the limiting value:
\[
v_x=\lim_{\Delta t\to0}\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}
\]

questions.prompt: If \(v_x=0\) at one instant, does the particle have to remain at rest?
questions.answer: No. \(v_x=0\) at one instant can occur at a turning point. The velocity can become nonzero immediately after.

questions.prompt: A position-time graph has a local maximum at \(t=6\,\mathrm{s}\). What is \(v_x\) at that instant?
questions.answer:
At a smooth local maximum, the tangent slope is zero:
\[
v_x=0
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t\), find all times when the particle is instantaneously at rest and classify whether the position is locally increasing or decreasing between them.
A particle has \(x(t)=At^2+Bt+C\). Given \(x(0)=2\,\mathrm{m}\), \(x(1)=5\,\mathrm{m}\), and \(v_x(1)=7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find \(x(t)\).
questions.answer:
\[
x(0)=C=2
\]
\[
x(1)=A+B+2=5\Rightarrow A+B=3
\]
\[
v_x=2At+B,\qquad v_x(1)=2A+B=7
\]
Subtracting the equations gives \(A=4\), so \(B=-1\). Therefore
\[
x(t)=4t^2-t+2
\]
